title: How Pond Slime Remembers
hook: Your brain needs billions of neurons to remember, but pond slime needs none.
script: Your brain needs billions of neurons to remember, but pond slime needs none. How does a single microbe recall where it was poisoned? When microbes survive a toxic environment, they alter internal iron levels like living scar tissue. That physical memory changes how they swim hours after the danger disappears. They learn without a brain. Even wilder, that stored experience passes directly down to four generations of offspring. Entire swarms inherit survival tricks from ancestors who faced threats they never saw.

captions: Could microbial memory change how we define intelligence? Would you call this real memory or pure chemistry?
Single-celled microbes can store memories and pass them down four generations without a nervous system.
The wildest adaptation in biology isn't teeth or claws. It is chemical memory.
